alternatives.root_cause: fraud-detection exhausted memory/threads and stopped processing while the container stayed up.
alternatives.why_not: Resource exhaustion usually shows itself first as rising latency or partial errors and then a crash/restart loop, which would produce some telemetry; a clean, instant drop to zero traffic fits a freeze better.

alternatives.root_cause: A flag flipped in flagd disabled or broke the fraud-detection consumption path.
alternatives.why_not: flagd is shared by ad, cart, recommendation and product-reviews, none of which alerted, and a flagged code path normally fails loudly rather than silencing all telemetry.

verdict.summary: The fraud-detection process is stopped/frozen — it still holds its socket and Kafka session but executes nothing, so it emits no spans or logs at all and trips the no-traffic alert.
verdict.reasoning: The only signal is ServiceNoTraffic on fraud-detection, and the blast radius is just fraud-detection plus its single dependency flagd. A complete absence of telemetry from one leaf service, with no error-rate or latency alerts anywhere upstream (checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy are all quiet), is the signature of a process that is alive-but-not-running rather than one that is failing requests. fraud-detection is a consumer-side service with no inbound callers in this graph, so a freeze produces silence rather than caller-visible errors — exactly what was alerted. flagd appears in the radius only because it is the dependency edge, and flagd itself is not alerting, which argues against a flag-path or flagd-outage explanation.
open_questions: Did fraud-detection emit any log line at all after onset, or is the log stream completely empty (freeze) versus complaining about unreachable peers (partition)?
Is the container still in Running state with no restarts, or did it OOM-kill/restart?
Is its Kafka consumer group lag growing while the member stays joined (freeze) or did it leave the group?
Did flagd's evaluation count for fraud-detection flags drop to zero at the same instant, or continue?
Any recent deploy or flag change touching fraud-detection in the minutes before 22:09:16?
